symbols.name: CachePayloadReader
symbols.summary: Builds an owned logical read handle over an acquired provider snapshot with bounded envelope, transform, and transfer state.

symbols.name: OpenAsync(ICacheProviderReadHandle, CacheReadOptions, CacheCollectionBinding, CacheRuntimeResources, CacheRuntimeTasks, TimeProvider, CacheAdmissionLease, CancellationToken, CachePayloadTransformRegistry, Action, ICacheProviderInfrastructureObserver, CacheObservationSlot)
symbols.summary: Adopts provider snapshot and transfer ownership, validates read capabilities, and removes registered persisted transformations.

syntax.content: public static ValueTask> OpenAsync(ICacheProviderReadHandle acquired, CacheReadOptions options, CacheCollectionBinding binding, CacheRuntimeResources resources, CacheRuntimeTasks tasks, TimeProvider time, CacheAdmissionLease transfer, CancellationToken cancellationToken, CachePayloadTransformRegistry transforms = null, Action validated = null, ICacheProviderInfrastructureObserver infrastructureObserver = null, CacheObservationSlot observations = null)

parameters.description: The acquired provider snapshot; this method disposes it on failure or transfers it to the returned handle.
The explicit full, seekable, or range read requirements.
The immutable collection policy and native capabilities.
The finite process and collection resource hierarchy.
The tracker for already admitted transfer tails and cleanup.
The transfer deadline clock.
The already admitted transfer lease adopted by the returned handle or disposed on failure.
Cancellation forwarded to initial envelope and range acquisition.
The optional code-approved reader registry for version-two transformation stacks.
An optional callback invoked after full-envelope validation, never for partial ranges.
Optional enabled provider-circuit observation for actual post-acquisition native reads.
Optional predeclared collection observations for late native failures.

returns.description: The owned logical handle, or a validation, capacity, capability, compatibility, or envelope failure.
